newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares recover off lows, await impulses.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares recover off lows, await impulses.

text.p: Norwegian shares recovered from early losses to close down but off intraday lows. Dealers said the market was relatively resistant given the sharp pre-weekend fall on Wall Street and the weak market in Japan.
Oslo's Total share index retreated 0.3 percent to end at 1,319.21 points, having hit an intraday low at 1308.59 points. Turnover was moderate at 841 million crowns.

"Investors are wary of the United States. Nobody wants to sell in case markets rebound, but nobody wants to buy in case of further drop," said a dealer. "More company results are due this week, people are waitng for new impulses one way or another."
Norway Seafoods, the world's largest catcher and processor of white fish, and metals producer Elkem will both present fist-half results on Tuesday.
Cruise liner NCL Holding ASA (NCL) was the most traded share in turnover terms at 95 million crowns. The stock gained 2.8 percent to close at 25.70 crowns.
Dealers said NCL was boosted by healthy passenger numbers and positive analysts' reports.
Construction and engineering group Kvaerener also put in a strong performance and advanced nine crowns in the As to 467 crowns and seven crowns in the Bs to 430 crowns.
